item.title: stats and limbs
item.description:
Most creatures have a race or race/class combo that determines their base stats & limbs. When creating a character, select a race and class from the list of playable races. This race and class combination defines most of your stats for you. See the following guide for all stats to calculate them. Physical ( determined by race and class ) Mental ( determined by race and class ) Defensive ( determined by race and class ) Effort ( 5 ) * You may select one main stat (Physical, Mental, Defensive) to increase by 1 point during character creation. These 3 stats in addition to the effort stat are used to perform combat actions. (New characters start at 5 effort.) Vitality has 3 parts to notate. Current Vitality, Maximum Vitality, and Attuned Vitality. Maximum Vitality is calculated by summing the vitality of your limbs. Current Vitality and Attuned Vitality both start equal to your maximum. Cur Vitality ( determined by race and class ) Max Vitality ( determined by race and class ) Att Vitality ( determined by race and class ) Choose any 3 items from their loot tables to start off with, write these items in your "possessions". These items can include armor. Your armor stat is whatever is listed on your armor. This armor value is the ratio of defensive effort spent to amount of damage reduced. When unarmored or in standard clothing, your armor stat is equal to the 'toughness' determined by your race. Armor ( determined by your equipped armor ) Limbs determine two things: maximum vitality and action slots. Each limb is formatted like the template below, showing the maximum vitality increase and the types of actions it can perform. Something's Appendage. [+3 MV] [Type] - Any custom action(s) this limb can perform.
During your combat turns, you will iterate through your action slots provided by your limbs, spending "effort" to perform an action of that type or one explicitly listed by the limb.
Now you are prepared for combat. Now just read to combat rules to learn how to roll the dice.
Read story and skills to learn everything you need to know about downtime.

item.title: combat
item.description: Enemy phase <=> player phase :: it's whoever started it first. Turn-order for players is in ascending mental stat value. Encouraged to sit around the table clockwise in that order to make things easy. Action-slots = your limbs. Type: Arm => Arm Actions: Attack/Use Defend Stabilize etc. Type: Movement => Movement Actions: Move Dash Status Effects follow the count + potency rules. Scar system list of combat actions

item.title: downtime
item.description: Chunks of non-combat non-roleplay time is spent doing "Downtime Actions" Craft Find Explore Rest etc. Use your skill bonusses on these downtime tasks to determine your effectiveness performing it. E.g. A crafted weapon is guaranteed to do (role) dmg per hit on average w/ it's basic attack. list of downtime actions

item.title: story and skills
item.description: A creature's story summarizes chapters of useful and pivotal experiences into "Cantos". Each Canto signifies a great deal of time, effort, and survival. As such, select 4 skills to gain or specialize in as a result of these experiences. Make sure to choose the proper skills that match your character's experiences and feats. These skills are used in "downtime actions" and roleplay. A new player-character must select a background to start their story.

item.title: character creation
item.description:
When creating a character, you will first choose from the list of playable races, which provide base values that your character will have in the main 3 stats: Primal, Mental, and Defense. In addition to these base values, you may choose one of these three main stats to allocate an extra point into. primalmentaldefenseAdditionally, you will mark down the limbs that your race provides. These limbs will determine what actions you can perform in combat, and your maximum vitality. Listed below are the remaining stats of the system apart from the main 3: Your expendable effort per combat round. Default effort value is 5 for all characters. A ratio of defensive effort to damage blocked. Your armor value is listed on your equipped armor. This stat is noted like asdef : dmg Vitality is your life-essence or health. Your character's vitality is capped by your Max Vitality, or "MV". Your maximum vitality represents how much life essence you can have. The "potential energy" of a living creature. Your MV is the sum of your limb's vitality values. Your attuned vitality is how much vitality your vessel is capable of containing without the adverse effects of vitality imbalance. Characters start with their attuned vitality equal to their max vitality. This grouping of Vitality stats can be noted as vit / max (attuned)
The story system keeps up with your character's life up to now, as well as what happens in each "Chapter" of the campaign. For character creation, simply choose a background and fill in your related stats. Feel free to flavor the background in any way you'd like, and bring up alternatives to the GM for alternative selections of skills.

item.title: noncombat
item.description: In noncombat, you will either be RPing, or passing larger chunks of time with "Downtime"During downtime, each player will state what they're doing by selecting a downtime action from below. These actions often apply the character's skills in any way applicable.Additionally, some scars may heal during downtime or resting, so check their descriptions. By training for 1 downtime period, you may increase your proficiency with a weapon, item, or limb. Cost: Reduce your vitality by your primal stat. story stufflist backgroundsList all skills here, and what type they are. Then, make skill-checks of the highest type add that much proficiency (by the lead amount.)Ex: Player has Physical as their strongest stat by 2pts => Physically proficient. +2 to Physical skills.
